newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-RANGERS SUNK BY THREE-GOAL GOTHENBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS SUNK BY THREE-GOAL GOTHENBURG.

text.p: Sweden's Gothenburg scored three second half goals on Wednesday to leave Glasgow Rangers facing an early exit from the European Cup.
The Scottish champions suffered a nightmarish second half to lose the first leg of the preliminary round 3-0 and now face a virtually impossible task at home in two weeks' time.
After a sleepy first half, with Rangers apparently looking for a draw, the Scots let in two goals in three minutes.
Rangers goalkeeper Andy Goram was helpless against a 20-metre scorcher from Stefan Pettersson in the 55th and equally abandoned by his defence three minutes later.
Gothenburg's Per Karlsson shot, Goram desparately palmed the ball out but it had already crossed the line.
One minute from the end Rangers' disastrous night was capped when substitute Peter Eriksson latched onto a through pass and drove past Goram.
The goalkeeper stood little chance with any of the goals, blame for which could be laid squarely at the feet of the hapless and disjointed Rangers back four.
Alex Cleland and English star Paul Gascoigne were both booked, the latter for a crude, lunging tackle.
